messages:
erin: Quick doc bug: API ref "generate" page has inconsistent param names. cURL uses "top_p" but Python SDK samples use "topP" (camelCase). People are copy/pasting and getting schema errors.

nate: yikes. we standardize on snake_case/underscores in REST examples, right? "top_p" is correct. SDKs map to languages' idioms but docs examples should show the raw HTTP payload keys.

 erin: exactly. PR #4991 accidentally replaced a few occurrences with the JS SDK style. I'll open a tiny fix to revert to "top_p" in code blocks that show raw JSON.

tess: also check the sample response: it currently has "topP" in the returned object which is wrong — server responses mirror the canonical snake_case names.

erin: good catch. I'll update curl, python, and the response JSON. adding a short note: "Note: SDKs may expose language-specific argument names; this page shows the raw HTTP JSON field names."

docs-bot: PR erin/docs-4991 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4991 1: fix generate examples to use canonical snake_case keys; update sample response; add SDK naming note. CI: docs build queued.

nate: can you also add a one-line migration tip in the generate migration guide for teams upgrading from older SDKs? some of our enterprise customers still rely on lower-level keys.

erin: added a line under docs/migration/generate.md: "When constructing raw HTTP payloads use snake_case keys (e.g., \"top_p\"); language SDKs may map these to idiomatic argument names."

tess: thanks. will run a grep for camelCase variants of param names and file follow-ups if any remain.

erin: OK merging after CI passes. thanks! :clap:
